newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Silver seen aiming for $4.55.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Silver seen aiming for $4.55.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Silver could make further progress on Friday towards an initial target of $4.55 an ounce following its successful breakout the previous day, technical analysts said.
But the upside for gold is less clear and further weakness might be seen after an indifferent close yesterday, they said.
SILVER
The break through the long defended $4.40 resistance yesterday was well supported technically and further progress is possible, according to technical analysts.
"There is a gap on the charts at $4.50-$4.55 and if they try to fill that it gives further upside potential," one analyst said.
Reaching $4.55 would pave the way to $4.80 and $4.90, levels seen briefly on spikes in May and June but not on a regular basis since April.
Locals on Comex finally took it on yesteray and drew the funds into the pit when buy stops were triggered, dealers said.

"Having taken so long to break upwards -- forming a triple bottom in the process -- look to some consolidation above $4.40 to confirm the move to the upside," said technical analyst Martin Squires at brokers Rufdolf Wolff and Co.
At 0750 GMT silver was indicated at $4.48/$4.50, unchanged from Thursday's close.
GOLD
The outlook was less positive for the yellow metal which has struggled with resistance at $328-$329 most of the week, analysts said.

"The outlook is not positive for gold. It needs to attract fresh buying," one analyst said, adding that this was not a glowing prospect with the strong dollar boosting the gold price in most major currencies and discouraging speculators.
Whether or not silver's revival provided a stimulus for gold is less than certain as the markets have been noticeably indifferent to each other for several weeks.
"Gold is a sell at $329-$330," said one dealer.
Techncially gold lacks direction and could continue Thursday's performance of drifting either side of initial support.
For spot, some analysts were targeting a return to $320.00.
"We feel the dowtrend remains intact until $338 (on December Comex) is successfully breached," said analyst Martin Squires at broker Rudolf Wolff and Co.
At 0800 GMT gold was indicated at $325.10/$325.60 about 80 cents above the Thursday close.
PLATINUM

The strike notice posted at South Africa's Impala Platinum mining and refining complex has helped to support an already tight and well backed price but platinum is running into resistance, analysts aid.
Initially there will be selling around the present level but the key resistance was at $440.00.
"If that is breached then we could see prices rallying like at the beginning of June," one analyst said.
Platinum fixed at its highest level in seven years on June 6 at $495.00 and was bid that day at $505.00.
Meanwhile support should be fairly robust at $410 and $400, the analyst added.
At 0800 GMT platinum was indicated at $432.00/$435.00, about $5.50 above Thursday's close.
--Brian Spoors London Newsroom +454 171 542 8058
